To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a DNA-binding protein with a molecular weight of 50 000 (P6) is synthesized in both untransformed and hamster sarcoma virus transformed cells; 2) P6 synthesis follows a pattern of synthesis different from the two other proteins (P7, molecular weight 70 000; P8, molecular weight 80 000) which are synthesized in the same cells; and 3) the pattern of P6 synthesis differs in the two cell types.
the synthesis of the DNA binding protein P6 is altered in virus-transformed cells.

a class of DNA binding proteins, including one with a molecular weight of 50 000, are synthesized in a pattern that is characteristic of the untransformed cell type, but is different from that observed for two other DNA-binding proteins in the virus-transformed cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a class of DNA binding proteins whose synthesis is altered in virus-transformed cells.
the regulation of DNA-binding proteins and their possible role in the process of cellular transformation.
the study of the synthesis of DNA-binding proteins and their possible role as regulatory proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
P7 and P8' are not involved in the transformation process.
the synthesis of P6, P7 and P8' is altered during the transformation of hamster cells.
the synthesis of DNA-binding proteins is altered by the transformation of cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

P6 is a protein that is synthesized in untransformed NIL cells at the time of DNA synthesis but is not synthesized in NIL cells transformed by hamster sarcoma virus, while P7 and P8'are DNA-binding proteins that are synthesized in both NIL and NIL-hamster sarcomas cells at the time when DNA replication is initiated.
the synthesis of P7 and P8' is not affected by virus transformation, whereas the synthesis of P6 in transformed cells is not affected by cell growth and division
the synthesis of the P6 protein is under the influence of growth factors, while that of P7 and P8'is under the influence of cellular DNA synthesis
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are differences in the synthesis of DNA-binding proteins between untransformed and hamster sarcoma virus-transformed cells.
there are differences between the patterns of synthesis of DNA-binding proteins between untransformed and hamster sarcoma virus-transformed fibroblasts.
the synthesis of P6 in synchronized NIL-1-hSV cells follows a pattern that is different from that in untransformed NIL cells.
